AMGN.rationale: Amgen presents a mixed but mildly attractive picture. On the positive side, Q1 2026 showed solid YoY revenue growth of +5.8% and EPS growth of +4.4%, with the company raising full-year revenue guidance to $37.1-38.5B. The P/E of 24.6x sits near the low end of its 365-day range (22.6-49.7), having compressed sharply from ~45x in April 2026, suggesting the market has already priced in significant concerns. Gross margins remain healthy at 68.3% and net margins improved to 21%. However, several headwinds temper enthusiasm: the QoQ trajectory is weak (revenue -9.8%, EPS -43.7%), the balance sheet carries $57.3B in debt with only $9.2B equity (D/E of 6.2x), and the denosumab franchise faces accelerating biosimilar erosion with 8+ competitors. The Tavneos FDA withdrawal challenge adds regulatory uncertainty. The MariTide obesity pipeline is a potential long-term catalyst but faces intense competition from Lilly and Novo Nordisk. The next earnings date (Aug 3, 2026) provides a near-term catalyst, but the fundamental picture of patent cliffs and pricing pressure limits upside. The stock's 13% decline over 3 months and valuation compression create some value, but the structural headwinds prevent a stronger conviction.
